Per-node counters ordering distributed events
The oscillator driving the processor
Time synchronised across hosts by protocol

answer_explanation: Vector clocks track event ordering across distributed systems without synchronized clocks.

question: What is CRDT (Conflict-free Replicated Data Type)?

options.option_value: A category of relational database engine
A structure whose replicas always converge
A category of application interface style
A protocol for moving bytes between hosts

answer_explanation: CRDTs ensure convergence without coordination in distributed systems.

question: What is the difference between push and pull models?

options.option_value: There is no real difference between them
Push: the server sends; pull: the client asks
Push is the slower of the two approaches
Only pull can deliver updates promptly

answer_explanation: Push model: server pushes updates; Pull model: client polls for updates.

question: What is event sourcing?

options.option_value: Storing current state only
Storing state changes as events
Database normalization
Data compression

answer_explanation: Event sourcing stores state changes as events, reconstructing state by replaying.

question: What is CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation)?

options.option_value: One model serving reads and writes
Reads and writes served by separate models
Copying the same data to more nodes
A convention for laying out endpoints

answer_explanation: CQRS separates read and write operations to different models for optimization.

question: What is event-driven architecture?

options.option_value: Callers wait for each reply in turn
Components emitting and consuming events
Work collected and run overnight in one go
Every call blocking until it completes

question: What is choreography in microservices?

options.option_value: One coordinator drives every step
Each service reacts to events itself
An operator moves the work along by hand
Steps driven by triggers in the database

answer_explanation: Choreography: services independently react to events without central orchestrator.

question: What is orchestration in microservices?

options.option_value: Each service reacts to events itself
One coordinator drives every step
An operator moves the work along by hand
Steps driven by triggers in the database

answer_explanation: Orchestration: central coordinator (orchestrator) manages service interactions.

question: What is strangler fig pattern?

options.option_value: A way of laying out database tables
Replacing the monolith one piece at a time
A policy for expiring cached entries
A method for spreading traffic evenly

answer_explanation: Strangler fig incrementally replaces monolith functionality with microservices.

question: What is bulkhead pattern?

options.option_value: Splitting stored rows across machines
Separate pools so one failure stays put
A policy for expiring cached entries
A method for spreading traffic evenly

answer_explanation: Bulkhead isolates components so failure in one doesn't affect others.
